title: Long ADBE — CFO Departure Oversell; AI Fundamentals Unbroken at $165-175
entry: Conditional — initiate on a confirmed volume-exhaustion candle at $162-175 (open June 15-16). A volume-exhaustion candle is defined as: a session where ADBE trades in the $163-175 range with volume below the June 12 announcement-day level AND closes in the upper 40% of the day's range. This signal confirms the panic sellers have been absorbed. Scale: 70% on the exhaustion candle close; 30% add if ADBE stabilizes above $165 on the next session. Do NOT chase above $178 on the first up-session — let the base form. This is a distressed-entry setup, not a momentum trade.
stop_loss: $155 daily close (~8% below entry midpoint $168.50) — implies the AI-substitution bear thesis is simultaneously validated (not just management instability), OR a second major C-suite departure (CTO, CPO) widens the leadership vacuum beyond a CFO replacement cycle, OR a data breach or critical AI product failure compounds the management vacuum
targets: $185 — partial gap-fill of the CFO-departure gap from $204 (June 14) to $168 (June 15); new CFO candidate announced or interim appointment confirmed; selling exhaustion confirmed over 3+ sessions; +9.8% from entry midpoint $168.50

$200 — full management stability signal: CFO named + Q3 FY2026 early Firefly AI ARR data shows no deceleration from Q2's tripling; ADBE re-enters the $200+ zone where institutional buyers pre-announced departures had been accumulating; +18.7%

$220 — ADBE re-rates toward pre-CFO-announcement levels as management vacuum resolves; Firefly AI ARR sequential acceleration confirmed in first post-departure guidance; the market recognizes the oversell; +30.6%
catalyst: ADBE fell to approximately $168 pre-market June 15 — its lowest level of 2026 — as the June 14 final trading day for departing CFO Dan Durn landed with continued selling pressure. The prior June 12 management instability position (long-adbe-management-instability-bottom) was stopped out today on this gap. However, the fundamental case that drove that position remains intact: Adobe Q2 FY2026 delivered non-GAAP EPS $5.96 (beat $5.81), Firefly AI ARR tripled year-over-year, and total revenue reached $6.62B vs. $6.45B consensus. A company with these fundamentals trading at ~$168 is being discounted for a single executive departure, not a fundamental impairment. At $168, ADBE trades at roughly 6.8x next-twelve-months revenue — the lowest multiple in three years for a software business with double-digit revenue growth.
thesis:
ADBE at $168 represents a category error by the market: pricing a permanent management impairment into a temporary leadership transition. Dan Durn's departure to Marvell — unusual but not unprecedented for a CFO to join a hardware company mid-AI-cycle — created a gap-down today that compounds the already-discounted valuation from Adobe's -30%+ YTD performance entering June. But the core business is empirically intact: Firefly AI ARR tripled sequentially, showing the AI substitution bear thesis has not materialized; enterprise subscription renewal rates remain stable; and the $25B buyback authorization signals board confidence in the capital allocation story. The $155 stop is 8% below entry — tight enough to enforce discipline, wide enough to allow for a day-two oversell (typically the most volatile session after a CFO departure gap-down).

The setup is specifically the volume-exhaustion entry. CFO departure gap-downs follow a predictable pattern: Day 1 (June 12) is the announcement, Day 2 (June 13) is the secondary selling by momentum funds hitting stops, and Day 3-5 is the exhaustion phase when retail stop-losses are cleared and the stock starts to stabilize. We are now at Day 3 (June 15 is the CFO's final day). The $168 level is the exhaustion target of this cycle: the gap from $204 (June 14 close) to $168 (pre-market June 15) is a 17.6% decline in 24 hours for a company that beat earnings estimates by 2.6% three days ago. The asymmetry between the fundamental trajectory and the price action is the edge.

The CFO replacement timeline is predictable. For large-cap software companies, the search-to-appointment cycle averages 45-90 days. Adobe's most likely path: interim CFO named within 2-3 weeks (probably the VP Finance or a known internal candidate), followed by an external hire announced in the August-September window before Q3 FY2026 earnings. Each of these announcements is a catalyst for the stock to re-rate toward $185-200 as the management vacuum closes. The position's 3-6 week horizon is designed to capture the first recovery leg (to $185 at minimum), not the full 4-month recovery cycle.

The counter-party is the fundamental bear who argues: (1) Dan Durn's departure to Marvell is a vote of no-confidence in Adobe's AI monetization strategy — he sees the same Firefly numbers the market does and chose to leave; (2) the 'freemium model' strategic shift signals pricing-power erosion; (3) ADBE at $168 still trades at 6.8x NTM revenue, which is not cheap for a company growing 10-13% annually in a rate environment where multiples compress. These are real risks, hence the 2% position size and $155 hard stop.
bull_case: Volume-exhaustion candle prints on June 15-16 at $162-175 with declining volume; stock closes in the upper 40% of range. Interim CFO announced within 10-14 days. Q3 FY2026 early-quarter data (available via management commentary) shows Firefly AI ARR sustaining the Q2 tripling trajectory. ADBE gaps to $185-195 on the CFO appointment news. Institutional buyers who were waiting for clarity (JPMorgan, BlackRock) begin accumulating below $175 as the management vacuum resolves. ADBE to $200 by early July.
bear_case: Volume does not exhaust on June 15-16 — a second down-day on expanding volume signals institutional distribution, not retail stop-outs. CFO search drags beyond 90 days; no interim appointment announced. An activist hedge fund files a 13D challenging Adobe's AI strategy and demanding a board seat. Stop at $155 triggered. Tail: a major Adobe enterprise customer publicly reports migrating to a generative-AI-native alternative (Canva Enterprise, Stability AI), confirming the AI substitution thesis that the market was discounting before the CFO departure.
invalidation: $155 daily close, OR volume-exhaustion signal does not fire on June 15 or June 16 (no entry without the signal), OR second C-suite departure announced within 5 calendar days of Dan Durn's exit, OR ADBE issues a guidance pre-announcement indicating Q3 Digital Media ARR growth below 8%
